# google_apihub_attribute

An attribute in API Hub is a name-value pair that can be attached to API Hub
resources, such as APIs, versions, and deployments, depending on the
attribute's scope. This resource manages user-defined attributes.
System-defined attributes are predefined by API Hub and can't be created or
deleted.


To get more information about Attribute, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/reference/apis/apihub/rest/v1/projects.locations.attributes)
* How-to Guides
    * [Manage attributes](https://cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/manage-attributes)
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/what-is-api-hub)

~> **Warning:** Changing `scope` or `data_type`, or decreasing `cardinality`, recreates the
attribute. Deleting an attribute also deletes all of its associations with
API Hub resources. Set `deletion_policy = "PREVENT"` to block accidental
deletion.
~> **Note:** An API Hub instance (`google_apihub_api_hub_instance`) must already exist
in the project and location.

## Example Usage - Apihub Attribute Basic


```hcl
resource "google_apihub_attribute" "default" {
  location     = "us-central1"
  attribute_id = "example-attribute"
  display_name = "Example String Attribute"
  scope        = "API"
  data_type    = "STRING"
}
```

## Example Usage - Apihub Attribute Enum


```hcl
resource "google_apihub_attribute" "default" {
  location     = "us-central1"
  attribute_id = "example-enum-attribute"
  display_name = "Example Enum Attribute"
  description  = "Initial enum attribute description"
  scope        = "VERSION"
  data_type    = "ENUM"

  allowed_values {
    id           = "value-1"
    display_name = "Value 1"
    description  = "First allowed value"
  }

  allowed_values {
    id           = "value-2"
    display_name = "Value 2"
  }

  allowed_values {
    id           = "value-3"
    display_name = "Value 3"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The display name of the attribute.

* `scope` -
  (Required)
  The scope of the attribute, which is the type of API Hub resource the
  attribute can be attached to. Possible values include `API`, `VERSION`,
  `SPEC`, `API_OPERATION`, `DEPLOYMENT`, `DEPENDENCY`, `DEFINITION`,
  `EXTERNAL_API`, and `PLUGIN`.

* `data_type` -
  (Required)
  The data type of the attribute's values. Possible values include `ENUM`,
  `JSON`, `STRING`, and `URI`.

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the API Hub instance, for example `us-central1`.

* `attribute_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID to use for the attribute, which becomes the final component of the
  attribute's resource name. It must be unique within the API Hub instance,
  4-500 characters long, and can contain letters, numbers, hyphens (`-`),
  and underscores (`_`).


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  The description of the attribute.

* `allowed_values` -
  (Optional)
  The list of allowed values, required when `data_type` is `ENUM`. An
  attribute can have at most 1000 allowed values. Once set, the list can't
  be updated to be empty. Removing an allowed value also removes it from
  any API Hub resources that use it.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_allowed_values).

* `cardinality` -
  (Optional)
  The maximum number of values the attribute can have when it's attached
  to an API Hub resource. Must be between 1 and 20. A cardinality of 1
  means the attribute is single-valued. Defaults to `1`. Cardinality can
  only be increased in place; decreasing it recreates the attribute.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_allowed_values"></a>The `allowed_values` block supports:

* `id` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the allowed value. It must be unique within the attribute,
  3-500 characters long, and can contain letters, numbers, hyphens
  (`-`), and underscores (`_`).

* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The display name of the allowed value.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  The detailed description of the allowed value.

* `immutable` -
  (Output)
  Whether the allowed value is immutable. Immutable allowed values
  can't be updated or deleted.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the attribute, in the format
  `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/attributes/{attribute}`.

* `definition_type` -
  The definition type of the attribute. Possible values are
  `SYSTEM_DEFINED` and `USER_DEFINED`.

* `mandatory` -
  Whether the attribute is mandatory for the resource type in `scope`.
  Only system-defined attributes can be mandatory.

* `create_time` -
  The time at which the attribute was created.

* `update_time` -
  The time at which the attribute was last updated.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


Attribute can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{attribute_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{attribute_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import Attribute using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    attributeId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_apihub_attribute.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import Attribute using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}"
  to = google_apihub_attribute.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), Attribute can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_apihub_attribute.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}
$ terraform import google_apihub_attribute.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{attribute_id}}
$ terraform import google_apihub_attribute.default {{location}}/{{attribute_id}}
```
